sqlQuery.name: Coords
sqlQuery.sql: -- parsed: the ID grammar is decomposed exactly once, here. Row count matches -- the injected id SQL exactly -- duplicates are NOT collapsed at this level, -- because WDK expects one output row per input ID row. -- -- NEVER write the id-SQL macro name in a comment in this file. WDK substitutes -- it by blind textual replacement, so it expands inside comments too; the -- injected SQL is multi-line, so it escapes the '--' and corrupts the statement -- (observed: "syntax error at or near WITH"). wdkQuery -showQuery does NOT -- reproduce this, because standalone it never expands the macro at all -- the -- failure only appears when a real answer runs. Refer to it in prose instead. WITH parsed AS ( SELECT t.source_id , t.project_id , split_part(t.source_id, ':', 1) AS strain , split_part(t.source_id, ':', 2) AS ref_seq , split_part(split_part(t.source_id, ':', 3), '-', 1)::integer AS ref_start , split_part(split_part(t.source_id, ':', 3), '-', 2)::integer AS ref_end FROM (##WDK_ID_SQL##) t ) -- ids: parsed + the resolved reference sequence. Note this CTE FILTERS, it does -- not merely project: an unknown ref_seq drops the row here, and this is now the -- ONLY place that check lives (the offsets subquery used to repeat the same -- dots.ExternalNaSequence lookup, costing a second index scan per PK and giving -- the "unknown sequence yields no record" rule two enforcement points). , ids AS ( SELECT parsed.* , ens.na_sequence_id , ens.taxon_id FROM parsed JOIN dots.ExternalNaSequence ens ON ens.source_id = parsed.ref_seq ) -- segs: the DISTINCT key set the offset sums are computed over. Required for -- correctness, not tidiness: if the injected id SQL ever yields a repeated source_id, -- summing over the raw set joins each indel row once per duplicate and -- GROUP BY source_id collapses them into one group whose SUM is multiplied by -- the duplication factor -- silently, with no error anywhere. Distinctness here -- makes the offsets independent of input multiplicity by construction. , segs AS ( SELECT DISTINCT source_id, strain, ref_start, ref_end, na_sequence_id FROM ids ) , offsets AS ( SELECT seg.source_id -- Boundary asymmetry is deliberate and load-bearing on the START side: -- '<' for the start offset. An indel exactly at ref_start lies INSIDE the -- segment, so it shifts the end but not the start. An off-by-one here is -- silent -- the coordinates just come out wrong, with no error anywhere. , SUM(CASE WHEN i.location < seg.ref_start THEN i.shift ELSE 0 END) AS offset_start -- The end offset needs no CASE: the '<= seg.ref_end' bound is enforced in -- the WHERE clause below, so every surviving row is in scope for the end -- sum. (An earlier revision wrote -- "CASE WHEN i.location <= seg.ref_end THEN i.shift ELSE 0 END"; that ELSE -- branch was unreachable -- verified 0 rows disagreeing -- and made the -- asymmetry above look like it lived in two places instead of one.) , SUM(i.shift) AS offset_end FROM segs seg , study.protocolappnode pan , apidb.indel i WHERE pan.name = CONCAT(seg.strain, '_Indel') AND i.protocol_app_node_id = pan.protocol_app_node_id AND i.na_sequence_id = seg.na_sequence_id AND i.location <= seg.ref_end -- Grouping on seg.source_id (the whole PK) makes one-row-per-PK true by -- construction; one protocol_app_node_id spans EVERY sequence of a strain, so -- grouping on coordinate fields alone conflated segments on different -- sequences and summed a foreign chromosome's shifts into both. GROUP BY seg.source_id -- NOT redundant, and not to be "cleaned up": it is here so that a strain -- name resolving to two protocol app nodes ON THE SAME SEQUENCE yields -- DUPLICATE rows per PK and a loud WDK error, rather than silently summing -- two strains' shifts. Provenance matters for the numbers here, because -- the two databases in play disagree by two orders of magnitude: -- genomicsdb_rebuild01 (a DIFFERENT, larger database, and where the -- original of this comment was measured): 126 strain names each -- resolve to two OR MORE protocol app nodes (122 to two, 4 to three; -- 256 nodes in all) that ALL already carry indel rows, so the -- ambiguity exists in that data right now. -- unidb_shu_a (the LIVE appDb, measured 2026-07-31): no ambiguity at -- all -- 452 '_Indel' nodes, 452 distinct names, 0 names spanning -- more than one organism, and (strain, taxon) resolving to exactly -- one node in 452 of 452 cases. -- So this detector is dormant here today and would NOT have been on -- rebuild01; keep it. What keeps it dormant even under the rebuild01 -- shape is the narrower invariant the join on na_sequence_id relies on -- -- no (strain name, na_sequence_id) pair is served by more than one node -- (0 on both). A data change that breaks THAT is what this fires on. , i.protocol_app_node_id ) -- Outer wrapper exists so strain_length is computed from the strain_start / -- strain_end columns themselves rather than by repeating their offset arithmetic -- (a SELECT cannot reference its own aliases). Do not re-inline it: a partial -- edit to one copy would yield a length that silently disagrees with its own -- start and end. SELECT coords.* -- Clamped at zero: a segment lying inside a deletion legitimately inverts -- (the reference bases do not exist in this strain), which would otherwise -- yield a negative length. strain_start/strain_end are deliberately NOT -- clamped -- the inversion (strain_end < strain_start) is the signal that -- StrainSegmentFeatureProvider rejects loudly (spec 5.3.2, 7). That class -- landed in ApiCommonWebsite a3c062e03, hardened in e5346e9c4: it rejects -- the inversion, rejects strain_start < 1, and asserts the strain_seq_id -- attribute agrees with the key computed from the primary key. So leaving -- these two columns unclamped is safe ONLY because that guard exists; if it -- is ever removed, an inverted segment reaches a FASTA lookup unflagged. , GREATEST(coords.strain_end - coords.strain_start + 1, 0) AS strain_length FROM ( SELECT ids.source_id , ids.project_id , ids.strain , ids.ref_seq , ids.ref_start , ids.ref_end -- OPAQUE key -- must match the dnaseq FASTA defline <sample>_<chrom>, -- written by dnaseq-nextflow bin/makeConsensusFastaFromVcfAndBed.py:233 -- (spec 2; that script is not in this checkout), and must NEVER be -- split back apart. The '_' is not a usable -- delimiter: measured on genomicsdb_rebuild01 (a DIFFERENT, larger -- database) over the 6,119 strain names carrying indel data, 1,494 -- (24%) themselves contain '_' (1_01_01, Af293_resequence2, -- China_LZCH-36, USGS_28834_1_NV), so "the first '_' ends the strain name" -- is false for roughly a quarter of strains. A consumer needing the -- strain or the sequence takes it from the primary key, where ':' -- delimits unambiguously: 0 strain names contain ':' (0 of 6,119 on -- rebuild01, 0 of 452 on the live unidb_shu_a), and the ID query -- refuses to mint an ID for a reference sequence containing one -- (10,704 dots.ExternalNaSequence source_ids do on rebuild01, though -- none of its 20,823 indel-bearing ones; on unidb_shu_a it is 0 of -- 160,581 -- see that query's gate 4 on ref_seq). , ids.strain || '_' || ids.ref_seq AS strain_seq_id , ids.ref_start + COALESCE(off.offset_start, 0) AS strain_start , ids.ref_end + COALESCE(off.offset_end, 0) AS strain_end , tn.name AS organism FROM ids -- Second silent row-drop point (the ids CTE is the other): an inner join, -- so a sequence whose taxon has no 'scientific name' row disappears with -- no record and no error. 0 affected today (0 sequences with a NULL -- taxon, 0 taxa missing a scientific name). Note the cross-query -- inconsistency this leaves: the ID query decides "does this sequence -- have an organism" via apidb.organism, this one via sres.TaxonName. -- They agree on all current data; nothing enforces that they keep -- agreeing, so a divergence would show up as records that pass the ID -- query and then vanish from the page. JOIN sres.TaxonName tn ON tn.taxon_id = ids.taxon_id AND tn.name_class = 'scientific name' LEFT JOIN offsets off ON off.source_id = ids.source_id ) coords
